items.title: Go from alert to post-incident review with Grafana Cloud IRM and AI
items.summary: You’ve got 10 minutes before your next meeting when your phone starts ringing. You’re being paged because the frontend is erroring with failed API requests.You open one tool to see what fired, then another to figure out what’s going on. You message a teammate in Slack to see if they’re noticing the same thing.That’s a lot of context switching, and it’s still how a lot of teams' incident response works today. Opening another tool and catching someone up takes time. Details can get lost when you manually copy context from one place to another.It doesn’t have to be this way. With Grafana Cloud IRM, you get on-call support, incident management, chatops in Slack or Microsoft Teams, investigations, and the Grafana mobile app, all connected through the incident record. Let’s follow the frontend incident from the first page through the response and post-incident review to illustrate how your team can start improving their processes today.The page already has contextWhen you get paged, you need to understand how serious the problem is and what to check first. With IRM, you’re starting with more than an alert name.When you open the alert group, it shows the affected service, the dashboard panel tied to the alert, its history, and how many individual alerts were folded into the page.Imagine the difference between “the frontend is exposing API errors" and “the frontend is exposing HTTP 500 errors from the adService, the issue has already flapped twice in 24 hours, and three related alerts are firing in the same alert group.”Figuring out what else is affectedNext, you need to figure out whether the frontend errors are isolated or part of something bigger, and whether the platform team is getting paged, too.A lot of teams will do this by bouncing between dashboards, service maps, observability data, and Slack or Teams.From the Slack thread, you ask Grafana Assistant, “What else is firing, and how is it related?”It uses the same alert context you’re looking at and posts the answer back in the same thread.Click Investigate this alert in the Slack message to get a quick summary of what’s firing and suggestions for what to check next.Everyone in the thread can see what Assistant found, including teammates who join the response later. If someone has a follow-up, they can ask @Grafana in the thread.You can ask it to help write a query to check the frontend’s error rate or find the dashboard you need. You can also give Assistant a service-specific playbook through Skills.Declaring the incidentOnce it’s clear this needs a coordinated response, you declare an incident in IRM.As soon as you do so, IRM handles a number of automated actions for you, removing the need for manual creation every time. You immediately have a dedicated Slack channel, a Zoom call, and an AI investigation that starts looking for the root cause.You don’t need to worry about the team remembering to create these components. The system does it for you.Keeping the messy stuffA lot of the useful information shows up in Slack before anyone knows if it matters.A teammate remembers a deployment from earlier and suggests it might explain the frontend errors. Someone else has a hypothesis about a dependency. Another person spots something weird on a dashboard.Usually some of that makes it into the incident record and the rest dies in Slack history.In IRM, a teammate can react to a Slack message with the robot emoji and drop it onto the incident timeline. The original message, author, and timestamp come with it.It doesn’t have to be a proven theory. The point is to retain potentially useful context while everyone is still figuring things out.Managing the incident from SlackOnce the response is underway, the incident commander is juggling roles, tasks, comms, other teams, and the actual investigation.That can happen in the incident channel without leaving Slack. You can assign roles, create tasks with quick actions, and sync those tasks to Jira or GitHub so they still exist after the incident is closed.If another team needs to get involved, you can page them from the same place instead of hunting down their on-call schedule. Even better, enter "@Grafana assistant - who is on call?"The incident owners post status updates that are shared in Slack and pushed to the mobile app so stakeholders can follow along.An investigation you can actually inspectThe AI investigation starts automatically when you declare the incident.It takes the context that’s already there (alert data, linked dashboard panels, the timeline, and anything people added from Slack), combines it with your actual data, and starts forming hypotheses about what caused the problem.The Assistant Workspace feature provides a collaborative environment for you to work alongside the agent and track what it's doing, finding, and thinking. You can add a hypothesis, reopen one that got dismissed, mark something disproven, or ask the investigation a question.
